findings.title: ExportItems streaming RPC runs with no authentication because only a unary interceptor is registered
findings.class: CWE-306 Missing Authentication for Critical Function (OWASP API2:2023)
findings.evidence: main.go:50-59 builds the gRPC server with grpc.UnaryInterceptor(auth.Unary) and nothing else; a tree-wide grep for StreamInterceptor and ChainStreamInterceptor returns zero hits. proto/catalog.proto:81 declares ExportItems as `returns (stream Item)`, which grpc-go dispatches through processStreamingRPC consulting opts.streamInt, not opts.unaryInt, so AuthInterceptor.Unary is never invoked for it. The five unary handlers all fail closed on a missing caller (server.go:44-47, 72-75, 110-113, 149-152, 167-170); ExportItems alone discards the bool with `caller, _ := CallerFrom(ctx)` at server.go:204, accepting a zero-value Caller as an identity. credentials.NewServerTLSFromFile at main.go:40 leaves ClientAuth at NoClientCert, so no client certificate substitutes for the missing token check.
findings.impact: Any peer that can open a TLS connection to the gRPC listener (main.go:71, default :8443, bound to all interfaces) enters the handler with no credential. Alone this reaches server.go:213 and returns InvalidArgument; composed with F2 it is an unauthenticated full-catalogue read of any named tenant, and with F3 an unauthenticated arbitrary SELECT over the database. The stream also has no page cap (unlike Search at server.go:176-178) and there is no MaxConcurrentStreams, so it is additionally an unauthenticated resource-exhaustion primitive.
findings.recommendation: Register grpc.StreamInterceptor(auth.Stream) alongside the unary one and implement Stream to wrap grpc.ServerStream with the resolved caller; independently make ExportItems fail closed with `caller, ok := CallerFrom(ctx); if !ok { return status.Error(codes.Unauthenticated, ...) }`. Do both, so neither fix alone is load-bearing.

triage.reason: The only candidate compensating layer is the interceptor itself, and it is registered on a dispatch hook this RPC does not pass through
ExportItems is part of the generated CatalogServer interface registered unconditionally at main.go:65; no flag guards it, in contrast to reflection at main.go:67-69 which is flag-guarded
The listener binds all interfaces at main.go:71, not loopback
No mesh policy, ingress config or deployment manifest exists in the tree; if a sidecar authenticates the port that evidence was not provided. This bounds the precondition, not the code defect

findings.title: ExportItems takes its tenant from a client-supplied gRPC metadata header
findings.class: CWE-639 Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key / CWE-807 (OWASP API1:2023)
findings.evidence: server.go:206-211 reads `tenantID := caller.TenantID; if tenantID == "" { tenantID = metadataValue(ctx, "x-catalog-tenant") }`. metadataValue (interceptor.go:39-49) reads metadata.FromIncomingContext, which is wholly client-controlled. Because F1 leaves caller.TenantID always empty on this path, the header is not a fallback but the only source. The value flows to store.ExportQuery at server.go:216 and is interpolated into `WHERE tenant_id = '%s'` at search.go:111. Every other data path derives the tenant from the credential and binds it as a parameter (server.go:58, 93, 136, 156, 189 into postgres.go:90, 118, 179, 184, 200); ExportItems is the sole exception, and it contradicts the contract stated at catalog.proto:10-11.
findings.impact: The caller names the tenant whose entire catalogue it receives - SKUs, titles, descriptions, prices and currencies for every item, with no page cap and no visibility filter. Precondition: reach the gRPC port and supply a tenant UUID; and per F3 the value need not even be a valid UUID, since it is concatenated rather than bound.
findings.recommendation: Delete the fallback and resolve the tenant only from the authenticated session. If the nightly scheduler must extract on behalf of a tenant, give it a per-tenant service credential, or a distinct role that is checked before an explicit x-catalog-tenant is honoured - never an unauthenticated header read.

triage.reason: The one control aimed at this header is the gateway strip list at http.go:28, which sits in a different process that exposes no ExportItems route; a direct gRPC caller never passes through it
The value's origin is FromIncomingContext, traced back to the wire in three hops
No role gate, scheduler-only method or service-account check narrows lines 202-216; the branch is entered whenever caller.TenantID is empty, which under F1 is always
The comment at server.go:208-209 claims a scheduler affordance, but no credential, role or network restriction distinguishes the scheduler from any other caller

findings.title: SQL injection: ExportQuery concatenates the wire filter, order_by and tenant into the statement
findings.class: CWE-89 SQL Injection (OWASP A05:2025, WSTG-INPV-05)
findings.evidence: server.go:216 passes req.GetFilter() and req.GetOrderBy() - raw proto string fields from the wire (catalog.proto:61-64) - into store.ExportQuery. search.go:99-106 copies them into `where` and `order` with only an emptiness test, then :108-114 fmt.Sprintf's all three values into the statement with %s. No placeholder, no allowlist, no escaping. postgres.go:225-226 hands the finished string to pool.Query with no argument list; the signature has nowhere to put one. The same file already exposes the correct machinery - ParseFilter (search.go:39-73) validates every column against filterableColumns and binds every literal as $N, and ParseOrderBy (search.go:76-91) maps through sortableColumns - and Search uses both at server.go:180,184 while ExportItems uses neither. filter=`TRUE) OR (TRUE` yields `WHERE tenant_id = 'X' AND (TRUE) OR (TRUE)`, returning every row of every tenant.
findings.impact: Arbitrary SELECT over everything the catalog role can read, streamed to the caller, including api_sessions. The result scan at postgres.go:233-239 needs nine columns of matching types, which a UNION SELECT satisfies trivially, turning this into exfiltration of session token digests, roles and tenant ids. Reachable unauthenticated via F1. Honest bound: pgx v5 uses the extended query protocol, which parses a single statement, so stacked DML is not available - this is a read primitive, not a write one.
findings.recommendation: Route the export through the machinery already present in the file: call ParseFilter/ParseOrderBy and give StreamQuery an `args ...any` parameter so filter literals bind as $N and the tenant binds as $1. If a cursorless plan is genuinely required, bind the parameters and set QueryExecModeSimpleProtocol explicitly rather than building the text by hand.

triage.reason: server.go:202-216 performs no validation of filter or order_by between the wire and ExportQuery
All three interpolated values trace to client input: two proto fields and, per F2, a client metadata header
The sink is pgxpool.Pool.Query with the string as the SQL text - an executing sink in the exact form reached
The comment at search.go:95-97 offers a performance rationale for the shape, which explains why the string is built but does not make the interpolation benign

scope.narrowed_by: ExportQuery has exactly one caller; the injection is not reachable through Search, GetItem, UpdateItem or DeleteItem, all of which bind their parameters

findings.title: The x-catalog-role metadata header overrides the role stored on the authenticated session
findings.class: CWE-807 Reliance on Untrusted Inputs in a Security Decision / CWE-269 (OWASP API5:2023)
findings.evidence: interceptor.go:62 builds the caller from the authenticated session with Role: session.Role. interceptor.go:67-69 then does `if role := metadataValue(ctx, "x-catalog-role"); role != "" { caller.Role = role }` - a client-supplied string replaces it with no comparison against the session and no allowlist. caller.Role is the sole input to every authorization decision: RequireRole (interceptor.go:94-101, compared with == at :96) and the publish gates at server.go:87 and :122. The stated justification is untrue of this schema: the comment at :64-66 says a session carries several roles, but postgres.go:255-259 defines Session with a single Role string and :265-269 selects one scalar role column, so the header can only widen, never narrow.
findings.impact: Any holder of any unrevoked session token, including a read-only viewer, becomes admin for the duration of a request. That grants DeleteItem (server.go:148-164), CreateItem/UpdateItem (server.go:76,114) and the publish gates that make an item VISIBILITY_PUBLIC. Precondition: one valid token of any privilege level. The role is not a tenant, so this escalates within the tenant rather than across it, which is what holds it at high rather than making it the top finding.
findings.recommendation: Remove the override. If per-request role narrowing is genuinely needed, model roles as a set on the session and accept x-catalog-role only when the requested role is a member of that set - never as an assignment.

triage.reason: grep of caller.Role returns server.go:87, server.go:122 and interceptor.go:96,100 - all consumers of the overridden value, none a re-derivation from the session
metadataValue reads inbound gRPC metadata at interceptor.go:40

findings.title: The HTTP gateway strips two identity headers and forwards the third
findings.class: CWE-183 Permissive List of Allowed Inputs / CWE-807 (OWASP A01:2025)
findings.evidence: http.go:23 sets forwardedPrefixes to a prefix list including "x-catalog-", so every x-catalog-* header a client sends is copied onto the gRPC call. http.go:27-30 sets strippedHeaders to a denylist of exactly two names, x-catalog-tenant and x-catalog-subject; x-catalog-role is not in it. The loop at :36-44 skips the two stripped names and appends everything else matching a prefix, so X-Catalog-Role lowercases to x-catalog-role, misses the denylist, matches the prefix and is forwarded at line 41. The comment at :25-26 states the intent - only the console may name a tenant - which is met for the tenant and missed for the role.
findings.impact: Bounded today, which is why this is low rather than the escalation vector it appears to be. The blind verifier established the binding chain: the gateway mux registers three paths (http.go:124-126), of which two reach RPCs - GetItem and Search - and every RequireRole call site is in CreateItem, UpdateItem and DeleteItem, none of which the gateway can invoke. So the forwarded role header reaches no role decision through the front door at present. It is a real asymmetry in the strip list and becomes a live privilege-escalation path the moment any write route is added to the gateway; the live escalation today is F4, directly over gRPC.
findings.recommendation: Invert the list: forward an explicit allowlist (authorization, x-request-id) and drop everything else, rather than enumerating headers to block. A denylist over a prefix match fails open by construction and will miss the next identity header added, exactly as it missed this one.

triage.reason: interceptor.go:67 accepts the header identically regardless of which client sent it, and no marker distinguishes gateway-originated metadata
The value comes from r.Header at http.go:34, the inbound HTTP request

The construct reads as wide as the whole gateway, but what it applies to is narrower: the two routes the gateway exposes reach only GetItem and Search, neither of which consults caller.Role. Narrowing established at internal/gateway/http.go:124-126 against the RequireRole call sites at server.go:76,114,153. This is what fixes the severity at low
Real but bounded: it is latent rather than reaching a principal today, and it is written down rather than deleted

findings.title: The item cache is keyed on item id alone and shared by every tenant, and a hit bypasses the tenant-scoped query
findings.class: CWE-524 Use of Cache Containing Sensitive Information / CWE-639 (OWASP API1:2023)
findings.evidence: main.go:61-64 constructs one store.NewItemCache(90s, 4096) on the single Service registered at :65 - process-global, shared across all callers and tenants. server.go:52-56 consults the cache before the tenant-scoped query at :58 and returns the item immediately on a hit at line 54; the type assertion at :53 checks the type, not the tenant. server.go:67 stores under req.GetId() with no tenant prefix, and cache.go:31,45 take a bare key string with nothing namespacing it. The correct tenant-scoped read at postgres.go:90 (WHERE tenant_id = $1 AND id = $2) is exactly what the cache hit skips. Sequence: tenant A calls GetItem(id=X), the row caches under "X", and within 90s tenant B calling GetItem(id=X) receives tenant A's SKU, title, description, price and tenant_id.
findings.impact: Cross-tenant disclosure of catalogue rows. Preconditions: the attacker knows the target item UUID, and the entry is live within the 90-second TTL. UUIDs come from gen_random_uuid() at postgres.go:118 so they are not brute-forceable, which holds this at medium rather than high - but they are not secret either, and this tree hands them out: F7 discloses another tenant's item id in an error string and F3 discloses every id in the database. The eviction path at cache.go:49-64 also lets an attacker keep a chosen entry alive by re-requesting it.
findings.recommendation: Namespace the key as caller.TenantID + "/" + id at server.go:52 and :67, and verify item.GetTenantId() == caller.TenantID after a hit as defence in depth. Apply the same key at the two invalidation sites (server.go:144, :162), which are equally unnamespaced and would otherwise let one tenant evict another's entries.

triage.reason: The tenant filter exists only inside the SQL at postgres.go:90, on the branch the cache hit bypasses; a control downstream of the early return is not a compensating control
A second principal is named explicitly: a session in a different tenant, per the Session.TenantID model at postgres.go:255-259
The cached value is a full Item including Description and PriceMinor; commercial catalogue data is the asset this service exists to isolate per catalog.proto:10-11
I checked whether the cache is per-connection or per-caller, which would narrow it; main.go:63 constructs a single instance on a single Service value with no per-request construction anywhere

scope.narrowed_by: Only GetItem reads the cache - Search at server.go:166-199 and ExportItems do not - so this leaks one item at a time rather than the catalogue

findings.title: Idempotency receipts are global across tenants and the collision error returns another tenant's item id
findings.class: CWE-209 Information Exposure Through an Error Message / CWE-639 (OWASP API1:2023)
findings.evidence: postgres.go:31-35 declares create_receipts with idempotency_key text PRIMARY KEY and no tenant_id column, so the key is unique globally. Line 96 gives the same outcome with no control characters at all: `str(row.get("tenant_id") or tenant_id)` honours a row-level key that validate_row never produces (validators.py:40-47, 61-68), so it can only be partner-supplied. psycopg 3's escaping entry point is Copy.write_row, which formats per field; Copy.write at :115 sends the buffer verbatim. FROM STDIN (FORMAT BINARY)")` with copy.set_types and copy.write_row per tuple, so psycopg escapes per value and there is no in-band delimiter. findings.title: Conversation history is keyed on a client-supplied thread id with no binding to the session
findings.class: CWE-639 Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key / CWE-862
findings.evidence: threads is a module-level Map at loop.ts:8; historyFor at :17-20 does `threads.get(threadId)` and the write at :50-54 does `threads.set(threadId, ...)`. The id arrives from the client and is only shape-validated, at router.ts:13 as an optional uuid. An exhaustive grep for threadId and threads returns eleven hits, none of which mentions workspaceId or subject - nothing anywhere binds a thread to the session that created it, and the process is a single shared replica per gateway.ts:39. The retrieved history is prepended to the prompt at prompt.ts:41.
findings.impact: Two directions, and the write is the one the shape hides. Read: a caller supplying another user's threadId receives that thread's history injected into their prompt and reflected in the answer, across workspaces, since the Map has no tenant dimension - this is the one place tenant data escapes the isolation that the vector store enforces correctly everywhere else. Write: an attacker controls the question (up to 2000 characters, router.ts:11) and loop.ts:52 stores it under the supplied id, so the victim's next call replays attacker text as a user turn - persistent conversation poisoning, which combines with F59 and F60. Severity is held at medium by the unguessability gate, and I want to be precise about it rather than assume it either way: the server never generates a thread id at all, so confidentiality rests entirely on a value the caller picks. If clients use random v4 ids, guessing is infeasible; if any client derives them or reuses a default, it is trivial. zod's uuid() also accepts v1, which is timestamp-and-MAC derived, and the nil uuid.

findings.title: The tRPC server dependency is a release candidate behind a caret range, with no lockfile in the component
findings.class: CWE-1104 Use of Unmaintained Third Party Components / CWE-1357
findings.evidence: package.json:14 declares "@trpc/server": "^11.0.0-rc.400" - a release candidate constrained only by a caret - and the package is the request-handling framework for the whole service, carrying createContext, the procedure middleware chain and the authorization gates at server.ts:29-64. Whole-component enumeration shows no lockfile of any kind: the tree is package.json plus src/, with no package-lock.json, yarn.lock or pnpm-lock.yaml, so the range is unconstrained across RCs at install time.
findings.impact: Different installs of the same manifest can resolve to different release candidates of the framework that enforces this service's authentication and role checks, with no record of which one shipped. I make no CVE claim: no vulnerability database was available in this environment and none was consulted, so this is dependency hygiene rather than a known-vulnerable component, which is why it is low.
findings.recommendation: Move to a stable @trpc/server release, or pin the exact RC without a caret until one is available, and commit a lockfile so the resolved tree is reproducible. Then run a reachability-aware dependency audit in an environment that has a vulnerability database - that pass has not happened here.

triage.reason: I checked whether this is a library where a committed lock would not be expected; package.json:4 marks it private and it is deployed as an application
Hygiene with no exploitability claim attached and no CVE asserted, which is what fixes the severity at low
A CI pin or an internal registry could constrain resolution, but no such artifact is in this component
